$comment: Scenario card style spec for scripts/art/cards.mjs. Prompt = subject + lighting + campaign $palette + $style. Subjects marked TODO block paid runs (dry runs still work). Draft: the orchestrator may refine after the C2 pilot.
$style: Painterly realism illustration, cinematic matte-painting key art, fully finished rendering with resolved detail on the subject, no loose sketch or speed-paint brushwork, atmospheric depth, clear value structure with one light direction; not comic, not photographic. 3:2 landscape composition. Horizon line in the lower third of the frame; sky fills at least the upper 60%. One anchor subject placed off-centre on a third of the frame; the subject's base sits near the lower-third line, fully in frame with clear margin on every edge. Calm negative space. No text, no logos, no readable screens, no faces. No people unless the subject names them; when named, at most two distant figures under 5% of frame height, mid-ground, never in the foreground. No fire, smoke, sparks or explosions; any warm accent is one small electric lamp or lit window. Soft film grain, oil-painted texture, soft edges, no cel shading or flat fills, consistent brushwork, cohesive set of scenario cards. Every satellite dish has a solid, opaque reflector with its feed at the focus on struts, and the whole dish stays in frame. No signature, watermark, artist mark or lettering anywhere, including corners. No steam, vapour, smoke, haze or plumes anywhere; the air is still and clear.

$palette.nats: New England cool blues and granite greys with a single small warm tungsten lamp accent.
$palette.nats-eu: North Atlantic slate, sea-green and amber.

1.title: First Day
1.subject: A nine-metre C-band dish stands on the left third of a Vermont hillside, its clean reflector angled above dew-covered grass. A gravel access path leads toward the pedestal, suggesting the start of a first inspection round.

2.title: Scheduled Maintenance
2.subject: A Vermont C-band dish rests in maintenance position on the right third of the frame, its feed assembly lowered toward an access platform. A work lamp catches disconnected waveguide flanges beneath the motionless reflector.

3.title: Weather Emergency Handover
3.subject: A nine-metre Vermont dish occupies the left third, its reflector collecting heavy snow while wind drives white curtains across the hillside. Ice thickens around the feed support, and the access road nearly disappears into the storm.

4.title: New Bird on the Block
4.subject: A Vermont C-band dish with a solid, opaque painted reflector sits on the right third, caught midway through a broad turn toward a fresh patch of sky. Its open azimuth track and newly displaced wheel marks make the change of pointing visible.

5.title: Interference Hunt
5.subject: A C-band feed horn on its struts at the focus of the Vermont reflector, mouth facing back into the dish, sits on the left third; its paired polarization ports and adjustment collar are sharply defined. Soft ambient light isolates the assembly against the night sky; no light beams or glow from the dish, with open ground and no structures in the foreground.

6.title: Old Faithful
6.subject: An ageing Vermont antenna pedestal occupies the right third, its weathered elevation gearing exposed beneath the cropped reflector. Fresh grease on the worn drive teeth suggests the repeated small corrections needed to follow a wandering target.

7.title: Uplink Validation
7.subject: A Vermont C-band dish seen from the front three-quarter on the left third, concave face toward the camera, the newly serviced feed on struts at the centre of the face, clean waveguide joints contrasting with older painted supports. Closed access covers and neatly secured cables suggest overnight work completed just before uplink validation. The site is empty, with no figures anywhere.

8.title: Night Shift
8.subject: A lone Vermont C-band dish occupies the right third under a deep starless sky, its pedestal washed by a single security lamp. Wet gravel and an empty access platform give the operating antenna an isolated, unattended feeling.

9.title: Morning Rounds
9.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the left third beyond a dew-covered fence, its nine-metre C-band dish silhouette rising from low ground mist behind the equipment hut. A freshly opened service gate and warm window glow suggest the first rounds of a newly qualified shift.

10.title: Customer Pass
10.subject: A Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third, its feed aimed steadily into a narrow opening between fast-moving clouds. Still, clear air around the rear amplifier housing suggests a sustained, demanding transmission window.

11.title: Planned Maintenance: Hand Off
11.subject: The Maine coastal dish sits on the left third above a rocky inlet, its reflector tracking steadily out over the grey sea, one warm lit window in the small equipment hut beside it as the station quietly carries another site's traffic.

12.title: Planned Maintenance: Return to Service
12.subject: The Vermont C-band dish stands whole on the right third, its feed horn on four struts at the centre of the concave face, the camera sees the face, showing a replacement waveguide gasket seated between bright, freshly tightened flanges. An empty access cradle hangs below the feed, the antenna poised to return to service; the full reflector and pedestal stay in frame.

13.title: Thermal Anomaly
13.subject: A Vermont dish on the left third with a grey converter box behind it, its grille clogged with dry leaves. The surrounding hillside remains still and cool.

14.title: Rain Fade
14.subject: A C-band earth-station dish on a Vermont hillside, a dark rain front sweeping in from the right, the air above the feed housing clear and still. The dish sits off-centre on the left third of the frame.

15.title: Frequency Coordination
15.subject: The whole Vermont C-band dish on the right third, the waveguide filter section visible on the feed at the focus, carefully aligned joints beneath. Thin parallel cloud bands beyond the dish suggest the narrow separation required between neighbouring transmissions.

16.title: Cascade Failure
16.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the left third, with uneven amber service light spilling from several open equipment bays. A motionless cooling fan behind an open bay door; still air, no vapour, beneath the dish suggests several independent faults demanding attention at once.

17.title: Solar Event
17.subject: A Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third in near silhouette, its pointing axis aligned with the low sun directly beyond the feed. A concentrated bright glare washes across the reflector, making the unavoidable solar interference visible.

18.title: Satellite Anomaly
18.subject: A medium shot of a Maine coastal C-band dish, the whole dish above the pedestal on the left third, its elevation drive exposed, the loosened protective boot hanging loose on the drive. Active gearing suggests an unexpected return to continuous tracking above the cold sea.

19.title: Train the New Hire
19.subject: A Vermont C-band dish occupies the right third above a training platform, the dish dominant in front of two tiny figures far behind the platform rail, each under 5% of frame height, observing its feed alignment. The reflector, struts and feed at the focus are clearly visible.

20.title: Dual Outage
20.subject: A Vermont C-band dish shown whole on the left third, the whole reflector visible in frame behind the iced feed, its heater jacket dark beneath a thick shell of rime ice. Wind-driven sleet streaks across the frozen reflector as the winter front consumes the hillside behind it.

21.title: Hostile RF
21.subject: A large satellite dish on its pedestal (the dish itself carries no lights) pointed at a low sky, with a distant unfamiliar mast and a single faint red beacon on the ridge line in the direction the dish is aimed. The mood is quiet tension. The dish sits on the right third of the frame.

22.title: End-of-Life Planning
22.subject: An ageing Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third, its patched reflector and faded protective coating catching weak light. Fallen leaves gather around the pedestal, giving the still-operating antenna the quiet gravity of a final assessment.

23.title: Emergency Bypass
23.subject: A Vermont antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its local manual-control compartment open beneath a stationary reflector. A portable work light reveals intact servo hardware and a disconnected controller module, suggesting movement remains possible despite failed automation.

24.title: Constellation Crisis
24.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the right third beneath an advancing wall of storm cloud, its operating dish sharply outlined against the last clear sky. Loose gravel and bent grass reveal the first gusts reaching an already pressured station.

1.title: First Light Over Galway
1.subject: A Ku-band LEO tracking dish on a green Galway headland, tilted toward a low pale sky, a small radome building beside it and a drystone wall in the foreground, the Atlantic beyond. The dish sits on the left third of the frame. The site is empty, with no figures.

2.title: Proving the Link
2.subject: A Galway Ku-band tracking dish occupies the right third, its precisely aligned reflector framed against a clear gap in layered Atlantic cloud. A temporary calibration fixture on the feed support suggests a station still being measured against its promised performance. The site is empty, with no figures.

3.title: Two-Way Street
3.subject: A whole Galway Ku-band dish on the left third, face toward the camera, its feed at the focus on struts, the transmit waveguide runs up the pedestal to the feed; no lamps on it. Fresh weatherproofing around the uplink housing suggests a receive station preparing to send its first authenticated command. The site is empty, with no figures.

4.title: Keys to the Bird
4.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third, its secured service entrance illuminated beside a closed, windowless communications enclosure. Fresh tamper seals and protected cable conduits suggest controlled access to the machinery behind a trusted command link. The site is empty, with no figures.

5.title: Shetland Comes Online
5.subject: A newly commissioned Ku-band dish stands on the left third of a Shetland headland, its pale reflector above wind-flattened grass. Fresh foundation gravel contrasts with dark peat, wet rocks and white surf below the headland, suggesting a remote station finally joining the network. The site is empty, with no figures.

6.title: Watch the Watchers
6.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the left third behind a wet perimeter fence, its access gate closed beneath a sharply defined security light. An empty service path and long fence shadows give an ordinary inspection an unusually watchful atmosphere. The site is empty, with no figures.

7.title: Moving Target
7.subject: A Galway tracking dish seen from behind on the right third, the feed hidden, a curved cable carrier looping around the azimuth base into a newly changed azimuth position. An older arc of scuffed gravel beneath the drive contrasts with the fresh direction of the reflector overhead. The site is empty, with no figures.

8.title: Night Passes
8.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the left third beneath broken cloud, its reflector turning above a dark radome building. One small pool of maintenance light on the empty headland suggests a solo operator carrying an entire night's pass schedule.

9.title: Morning Constellation
9.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third above a misty Atlantic inlet, with its tracking dish already raised from stow. Pale light catches dew on the perimeter fence as a busy day of constellation contacts begins. The site is empty, with no figures.

10.title: Priority Tasking
10.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the left third, tipped low toward a thin strip of sea beneath heavy cloud, the headland rising close on either side so the narrow pass window feels tight. The site is empty, with no figures.

11.title: LEOP: Launch Day
11.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish stands on the right third, its reflector searching just above an empty Atlantic horizon. A wide expanse of pale sky surrounds the small antenna, suggesting the uncertainty of acquiring a spacecraft on its first orbit. The site is empty, with no figures.

12.title: LEOP: Commissioning
12.subject: A whole Galway Ku-band dish on the left third, seen from behind with the feed hidden; a calibration coupler box on the pedestal, folded cover against the support. A temporary protective cover lies folded against the support, suggesting final acceptance work before operational imagery delivery. The site is empty, with no figures.

13.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
13.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the right third, tilted almost vertically with its elevation mechanism close to the zenith limit. Weather staining around the feed housing adds a second visible concern to the difficult overhead tracking geometry. The site is empty, with no figures.

14.title: Atlantic Low
14.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish stands on the left third as dense rain turns to sleet across the headland. Icicles and meltwater drip from the feed cover while a dark Atlantic cloud shelf closes over the reflector's low pointing direction. The site is empty, with no figures.

15.title: Rotation Day
15.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the right third, its antenna lowered between contacts beside a securely closed communications shelter. A narrow break in racing clouds briefly illuminates the service entrance, suggesting a short interval for a coordinated security change. The site is empty, with no figures.

16.title: Cascade
16.subject: A Shetland antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its cooling compartment open beneath a steeply raised Ku-band reflector, the whole dish in frame. One tiny back-turned technician far off near the lamp post, under 5% of frame height, walks toward the stalled fan while wind strains the loose access cover.

17.title: Unusual Activity
17.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the left third, its quiet radome and closed entrance reflected in rain-dark paving. A security lamp leaves the outer fence in shadow, suggesting subtle activity beyond an otherwise routine overnight watch. The site is empty, with no figures.

18.title: Dirty Spectrum
18.subject: The whole Galway Ku dish on the right third, its small feed horn on struts at the reflector focus, beneath a dry reflector while an offshore rain band remains in the distance behind. An attached diagnostic coupler suggests repeated interference checks under weather that cannot explain the persistent degradation. The site is empty, with no figures.

19.title: Frequency Agility
19.subject: A large Ku tracking dish on the left third, matte grey opaque reflector, evenly lit, feed at focus on struts with compact tuning housing and protected RF connections visible. Suggesting the need to keep a command path usable as conditions change. The site is empty, with no figures.

20.title: False Time
20.subject: The sky above Galway fills the frame, with a few fading stars low in the right part of the dawn sky, blending smoothly with the sky; no panels, seams or hard edges, over a low coastal silhouette. Faint doubled star trails suggest a trusted timing reference slipping away from the true sky. The site is empty, with no figures.

21.title: Knocking on the Door
21.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the right third, its communications shelter sealed behind a secondary locked solid steel barrier. A narrow shaft of light reaches the protected cable entry, concentrating attention on the boundary guarding the command path. The site is empty, with no figures.

22.title: Connecting the Dots
22.subject: One Galway headland site seen from fence level: one tracking dish, with conduits and fence converging at its foundation. Receding cloud reveals the whole installation clearly, suggesting separate incidents finally understood as one connected pattern. The site is empty, with no figures.

23.title: Dark Passes
23.subject: A Galway tracking pedestal occupies the right third beneath the whole dark reflector in frame, faint against the night sky, its normal service lights extinguished. A single portable lamp illuminates the manual-control compartment, suggesting one essential command must survive a night of simultaneous failures. The site is empty, with no figures.

24.title: North Atlantic Storm
24.subject: A tracking dish and a small equipment hut on a storm-lashed Atlantic headland, sleet slanting across the frame, waves breaking on dark rocks, one warm lit window in the hut. The dish sits on the right third of the frame. The site is empty, with no figures.

25.title: Site Orientation
25.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the left third beyond an open pedestrian gate, with a clear inspection path following the fence toward the radome. The empty route suggests the start of a deliberate review of the station's defences. The site is empty, with no figures.

26.title: Baseline Check
26.subject: A whole Galway dish on the right third with its pedestal cover open, grey weathered paint, the whole dish in frame; inside the cover one conspicuously fresh cable among older, neatly secured runs. Cool condensation on the housing suggests a pre-pass check catching an unexplained configuration change. The site is empty, with no figures.

27.title: Removable Media
27.subject: A Galway antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its controller service compartment open with a small removable drive still inserted in the maintenance port. An unattended tool roll rests below, suggesting an unverified firmware transfer interrupted before installation. The site is empty, with no figures.

28.title: Vendor Session
28.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third, its maintenance-room window unexpectedly lit while the tracking dish remains stowed. The locked gate and empty access road suggest remote activity occurring without an authorised visit. The site is empty, with no figures.
